newsitem.title: ITALY: OLYMPICS-SICILY SCOLDS GREEK MINISTER OVER MAFIA.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SICILY SCOLDS GREEK MINISTER OVER MAFIA.

text.p: Sicily, traditional mafia stronghold and host of this month's World Student Games, has stepped into a sharp war of words between Rome and Athens, rival bidders for the 2004 Olympics.
Officials from the Mediterranean island said on Wednesday Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos had an outdated view of Italy and Greece's transport network was stuck in the 1960s.
The officials were responding to comments made by Pangalos on Tuesday in which he accused Italy of exporting the mafia throughout the world.
Although Pangalos made no specific mention of Sicily, his comments touched a raw nerve in an island eager to shrug off its murky reputation for clan warfare.

"It seems to me the Greek minister is out of date with his thinking," said Antonino Strano, minister for tourism in the Sicilian regional government. "He's got an idea of Sicily as it was 30 years ago."
"He's not taken any notice of the incredible progress our land has made in getting rid of the Mafia."
Leoluca Orlando, mayor of Sicilian capital Palermo, said Pangalos should come to the island during the Student Games, which start on Tuesday, to see it for himself.
"He'll understand Sicily is a hospitable land and not a place of drive-by shootings," Orlando said.
Strano said Greece's transport system, a key factor in Athens' bid to host the 2004 Olympics, was as outdated as Pangalos' views.
"I was in Greece for the world athletics championships this month and I thought Greece was 30 years behind on transport. We are right behind Rome's candidature for 2004."

Rome and Athens are favourites to win the right to host the Games. The other bidding cities are Stockholm, Cape Town and Buenos Aires. The International Olympic Committee will name the successful candidate on September 5.
